corrected_findings: Helper publication uses one prefix scan per definition instead of a repeated full lookup for each helper.
Stored answer files are checked for completion and content corruption before commit.
Temporary decoding preserves empty lists instead of sending them as JSON null.
Container executable permissions no longer depend on the build user umask.
limits: BloodHound is stopped during calculation and publication; application queries are unavailable then.
No 100-million-edge demonstration. Resource budgets fail safely but are not a hard total-memory cap.
The final publication is one transaction; batching does not remove database transaction costs.
Container times are small-fixture measurements, exclude database memory, and are not a controlled backend performance comparison.
Helpers are not automatically deleted. A lost commit acknowledgement requires inspection.
